list: The official 55 trophies, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles (names, descriptions and grades agree on both), frozen 2026-11-18
note: Names and descriptions are shown exactly as PlayStation publishes them. Every guide is written in our own words for this entry, drawn from the official description unless a named source says more. Where no source pins down a place or a step, the guide says so instead of inventing one. The game released 2026-11-19 and nothing here has been checked in-game.

trophies.guide: This is the platinum: it pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is no separate task behind it. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap rather than a trophy to chase on its own. The real gate is A Long Road, the gold for 100% completion, so plan around that from the start and use this tracker to watch the count climb. Everything else in this guide exists to get you here.

trophies.guide: Finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission, and this pops. It is the first story trophy and the gentlest one: just play the opening as the game teaches it, without worrying about style or speed. Nothing here can be missed — the mission is mandatory and always available at the start of a playthrough. If it has not popped, you have simply not finished the mission yet.

Treat it as the first real milestone on the road to the platinum, and while you are in Chapter 1, start the meditation spots for Positive Mental Attitude — one of them is reported to disappear when the chapter ends.

trophies.guide: Attain 100% completion — the hardest trophy in the list and the real gate for the platinum. In Rockstar games, 100% means the story plus a set list of side content: missions, activities and collectibles tracked on the in-game stats screen. The official description does not spell out which items count, and no source used here pins down the full checklist, so treat the in-game 100% display as the authority: finish the story, complete the stranger strands, then mop up by category — collectibles, activities, races and challenges — checking the percentage after each block. Do not expect this to pop until the very end of a completionist run.

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunts are the jumps, airtime and near-miss driving the game counts as you drive around Leonida, so this is a grind that accumulates across the whole playthrough rather than a skill test. It will climb naturally if you drive fast, take jumps and chase the stunt jumps scattered around the map — but if you mostly fast-travel or drive carefully, the count will lag, so deliberately hunt jumps and ramps in the open-world stage. Nothing about it can be missed: the count never resets.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida — 18 spots, per PSN. This is the one trophy reported as possibly missable: GTABase and PowerPyx flag it, and the first meditation is Lucia's on the balcony at Jason's house in Chapter 1, reported to disappear once that chapter ends. So start in Chapter 1, meditate at every spot you find as you travel, and never walk past a meditation spot thinking you will come back after the story. The other 17 spots are not reported to vanish, but the safe play is to clear them during the story anyway. If you are already past Chapter 1 and missed the first spot, that is the one to check first.

trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. You need your partner beside you, a 4-star wanted level, and then a clean escape — lose the cops, do not get caught, do not die. The practical way is to build heat with your partner in the car, then break line of sight and hide until the stars clear. Doing it with your partner is the requirement, so do not try it solo. It is repeatable, so if the escape fails, build the heat again.

The chain is the hard part: three robberies in a row, partner with you, and the wanted level must stay on the whole time — if it drops to zero, the chain breaks and you start over. Plan a route of three close shops, hit them quickly, and keep moving between them. Expect a few failed runs while you learn the spacing; it is repeatable, so treat each attempt as practice.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-motion aiming mode, and the trophy needs five takedowns inside one activation — so set it up: find a group of five or more enemies, trigger Focus with a clear line on them, and drop them fast before the meter runs out. A busy firefight with clustered enemies is the right stage; a lone enemy wandering in the open is not. If the fifth falls just after Focus ends, it does not count — reload the attempt and try a denser group.

The description names the place and the drink, so the task is simple once you are there. It is a nice breather between the loud trophies, and it cannot be missed: the beach and its bars are always open.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The image is pure GTA: drive a car straight through a showroom's glass and out the other side. Find a vehicle showroom, get a car inside or lined up at it, and smash your way out through the front. The description gives no showroom name, so any showroom should do — the classic style is the point, not the address. Expect a wanted level and a broken car; that is part of the charm.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by. A drive-by is an attack from a moving vehicle, and melee means doing it up close with a melee weapon instead of a gun: drive past someone and knock them down with a melee swing from the car. The word 'bowl' is the bowling pun — knock them over like pins. Pick a slow drive past a pedestrian, swing as you pass, and keep moving. It is repeatable, so if the first swing misses, circle around and try again.

trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty money you pick up from robberies and heists, and your contacts clean it for a cut. The trophy counts what you earn from laundering — $250,000 in total — so the method is to keep robbing, keep laundering, and let the total climb. It pairs directly with the robbery trophies: every vault, truck and shop job feeds bills into the pipeline. Track the total in the relevant menu and keep the pipeline running until it pops.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. This is the shopper's trophy: buy clothes, weapons, food, car mods — anything the shops of Leonida sell — until the lifetime total hits $100,000. It climbs alongside normal play, since weapons and clothes are useful anyway, and it pairs with the laundering trophy: clean money in, spend it in the shops. If you are near the end of a run and still short, spend the surplus on the most expensive items you can find rather than hoarding cash.

trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — 8 of them, per PSN. Garages are properties you buy to store vehicles, and you need all eight owned. That means money and map coverage: find each garage for sale, buy it, and move on. It pairs with the vehicle trophies, since more storage means more of the 100 vehicles you discover can be kept. Work through them in the open-world stage once your funds allow, and check the property menu to see which ones are still unowned.
